items.title: George Masso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997
items.q: I said to Vic, “Vic, do you want me to mark your part?” He says, “No, George, I wasn’t going to hold it very long anyway.”

ctx.x: —without even trying. Well we were playing this particular Hoagy Carmichael tune. It was a Hoagy Carmichael concert. And Dick Sudhalter was leading the band, and he didn’t like the way it ended. There was an ending, and he thought well you know, let’s hold it all out, let’s hold the ending, and we put a fermata over it, you know this line that means you hold it until you’re cut off. So everybody marks a fermata , but Vic doesn’t mark the spot or anything, he’s just sitting there. So we try it with the fermata ,…
It sounded like he was a little tired from a lot of road work over the years.
